summary: TradingKey reported that NVIDIA invested $5 billion in Intel; the item gives no transaction date.
TradingKey reported that NVIDIA selected Intel Xeon 6 as the host CPU for DGX Rubin AI systems; the item gives no selection date.
Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan said Xeon 6 serves as an orchestration layer and control plane, and that the inference CPU-to-GPU ratio is shifting from 1:8 to 1:1; the statement date is not specified.
NN, Inc. announced in late June 2026 that it would add 47 machine centers for liquid cooling production at its Wuxi, China plant for NVIDIA AI data center racks.
NN said 100% of the new Wuxi capacity was already pre-sold under multi-year, multi-product awards as of late June 2026.
NN targeted US$80–US$90 million of accretive new business in 2026 from the expansion.
Fox News reported on 2026-07-01 that Corning was ramping up optical-fiber production amid rising AI-infrastructure demand.
NVIDIA and Corning partnered earlier in 2026 to build three advanced optical manufacturing facilities in North Carolina and Texas.

The three-facility Corning-NVIDIA project was expected to create more than 3,000 jobs across North Carolina and Texas and expand Corning's U.S. optical manufacturing capacity tenfold; the report gave no completion date.
Fox News reported that Taiwan-based Wistron was establishing AI-supercomputer manufacturing operations in Texas for NVIDIA; the report did not quantify the jobs or give a date.
Nvidia said it is looking to give developers token credits in exchange for a share of their future sales; no amount or timeframe was specified.
NVIDIA said its model lets AI clouds procure NVIDIA infrastructure with revenue sharing and credit support; NVIDIA plans to earn product revenue and a share of cloud revenue on supported capacity.
Firmus is building a DSX AI factory campus in Batam, Indonesia, expected to scale to 360 megawatts and up to 170,000 NVIDIA GPUs.
Sharon AI disclosed on 2026-06-12 that its agreement runs for six years and covers 72 MW of new Australian data-center capacity, scaling to as many as 40,000 Grace Blackwell GB300 GPUs.
Firmus is building a DSX-aligned campus in Batam expected to scale to 360 MW and house up to 170,000 Nvidia GPUs.
Tom's Hardware reported that Nvidia participated for $30 billion in OpenAI's $110 billion funding round and backed xAI's $20 billion Colossus 2 financing.
Jensen Huang estimated that U.S. AI companies spend $60 of every $100 on Nvidia GPUs; no period was specified.
The authors reported a forecast that Nvidia GPU shipments would grow 26 percent per year; the forecast period was not specified.
Jensen Huang set expectations for $1 trillion in orders for Vera Rubin and Grace Blackwell chips through 2027.
Tom's Hardware reported that resistance had led to delays or cancellations of at least 75 projects in the first quarter of 2026.
Sharon AI plans to deploy up to 40,000 Grace Blackwell GB300 GPUs; no deployment date was given.
Firmus is developing an Indonesia campus that could support approximately 170,000 GPUs and 360 MW of power capacity; no completion date was stated.
DatacenterDynamics reported that Firmus was deploying 170,000 GPUs in Batam, Indonesia, and Sharon AI was deploying 40,000 GB300 GPUs; no completion date was given.
Nvidia said in June 2026 that it aimed to raise debt; unnamed sources said the amount could be at least $20 billion.
Nvidia said it intended to use proceeds from the debt offering for general corporate purposes, including repaying and refinancing existing debt; no amount or period was specified.
Sharon AI plans to deploy up to 40,000 Nvidia Grace Blackwell GB300 GPUs; no deployment date was specified.
Firmus Technologies is developing a campus in Batam, Indonesia, planned for capacity of up to 170,000 Nvidia GPUs and 360 megawatts of power; no completion date was specified.
Jensen Huang said Nvidia’s China market share had fallen to zero since the Biden administration first imposed AI-chip export controls in 2022.
Nvidia estimated that Huawei sold 200,000–450,000 AI chips in calendar 2024 and would sell 1 million in calendar 2025.
Nvidia estimated that SMIC would make more than 700,000 Huawei Ascend 910C chips by the end of 2026, with monthly production reaching 50,000.
Nvidia’s report projected that SMIC would produce several million Huawei 910B chips by 2027.
Chris McGuire estimated in a December report that 800,000 Huawei Ascend 910C chips in 2025 would equal 5.3% of Nvidia’s total chip-production processing power that year.
Chris McGuire estimated that Nvidia’s performance lead would grow even if Huawei made 2 million AI chips in 2026 and 4 million in 2027.
Reuters reported that Huawei had stockpiled 2–3 million AI chips made by TSMC and obtained through illegal diversion by Sophgo; Nvidia’s report cited that reporting.
The Wire stated that U.S. export controls require companies such as TSMC that use American technology to comply, effectively preventing chip sales to Huawei.
Lennart Heim said the reported 2–3 million Huawei chip stockpile was small relative to more than 60 million U.S.-produced 910C-equivalent chips from January 2025 through the end of 2026.
Epoch AI estimated Huawei had 6% of worldwide AI-chip sales in Q1 2026, or half that share after adjusting for its chips’ lower power.
Huawei introduced its 950PR chip in March 2026 and was preparing to launch another chip later in 2026.
Lennart Heim said Huawei’s 950PR and planned chip would not match H200 quality because they have slower memory.
NVIDIA removed the AI Enterprise subscription requirement for Omniverse development, production use, and redistribution; the documentation says the change took effect in May 2026.
NVIDIA posted an announcement about the Omniverse licensing change to its Developer Forums on July 1, 2026.
Under the new terms, unsubscribed users receive community-channel support, while organizations seeking enterprise support SLAs continue to buy AI Enterprise through resellers or CSP marketplaces.
Sharon AI raised $1.6 billion in a June 2026 private placement and partnered with VAST Data for 600PB of storage infrastructure supporting roughly 100,000 GPUs.
IREN secured a five-year $9.7 billion AI cloud contract with Microsoft in November 2025.
IREN signed a $3.4 billion contract for AI cloud services with Nvidia in May 2026.
In March 2026, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said he expected Blackwell and Vera Rubin chips to generate $1 trillion in sales from then through the end of 2027.
Nvidia management said the company thought it could generate nearly $20 billion in CPU sales.
Wall Street consensus estimated Nvidia would earn adjusted EPS of $8.97 in FY2027.
The author says Nvidia’s GPU-and-CPU superchip for personal computing is set for release in fall 2026.
The author characterizes the CPU market Nvidia is targeting as worth $200 billion; no period is specified.
SemiAnalysis said on 2026-07-05 that NVL576, which links eight racks, was likely to be delayed or limited to small volumes.
CNBC reported on 2026-07-05 that a backup plan to bolt two current-generation Nvidia racks together had been scrapped after cloud customers rejected the design as awkward and costly to operate.
SemiAnalysis said the backup plan to connect two current-generation racks had been cancelled following heavy pushback from cloud service providers and hyperscalers.
SemiAnalysis said on 2026-07-05 that Nvidia had no proven way to expand Rubin Ultra's scale-up world size and predicted this could give AMD and Google a technical opening in the high-end market.
SemiAnalysis projected Nvidia data-center compute revenue in the second half of FY2027 at 20% above Wall Street consensus.

US authorities suspect a company involved in Thailand's national AI efforts helped smuggle billions of dollars' worth of Super Micro servers containing advanced Nvidia chips to customers in China, including Alibaba; reported 2026-07-06.
SemiAnalysis says market estimates for Nvidia's shipments and revenue in the second half of 2026 are materially below its supply-chain tracking estimates.
SemiAnalysis forecasts more than $7 trillion of AI debt outstanding by 2029, driven by AI IT and data-center capital needs.
SemiAnalysis forecasts annual AI capital expenditure, including IT equipment and data centers, will exceed $2 trillion in calendar 2028.
SemiAnalysis forecasts cumulative AI capital expenditure of about $11.1 trillion from 2024 through 2029 and says credit markets will be its main funding source.
SemiAnalysis says five years is the most common period for long-term take-or-pay compute contracts backed by hyperscalers.
SemiAnalysis says that, as of July 6, 2026, lenders require an offtake contract or investment-grade hyperscaler backstop to provide debt financing.
SemiAnalysis forecasts AI debt-financing needs will quickly exceed the size of other U.S. asset-backed markets, based on its GPU shipment and data-center capex forecasts.
SemiAnalysis estimates AI debt financing at hundreds of billions of dollars in 2024 and 2025 and forecasts about $7.1 trillion by 2029.
SemiAnalysis says data-center supply improved considerably by early 2026 and chip production became the limiting constraint.
SemiAnalysis says financing had become one of the most significant obstacles to broadly expanding large-scale compute by mid-2026.
SemiAnalysis says CoreWeave's fixed-rate tranche yield of 5.9% was about 90 basis points wider than Meta's approximately 5.0% five-year bond yield.
SemiAnalysis cites an approximately 10% yield on CoreWeave's five-year unsecured bonds.
SemiAnalysis says CoreWeave paid 5.9% on the fixed-rate tranche of its $8.5 billion DDTL 4.0 delayed-draw term loan, which Meta backstopped.
SemiAnalysis estimates a top Neocloud would pay an additional 4% interest for unsecured funding of a cluster rented to a broad customer base on shorter terms.
SemiAnalysis models PBT margin falling from 14.8% to 5.4% when all-in funding cost rises from 5.62% to 10%.
SemiAnalysis says banks generally seek at least 1.3x debt-service coverage, particularly in the first years of a GPU financing agreement.
SemiAnalysis says a 1.3x debt-service coverage threshold typically corresponds to a 70–80% loan-to-value ratio.

SemiAnalysis expects initial lending to Neoclouds to price wider than five-year hyperscale-backstopped loans at roughly SOFR plus 225 basis points, or 5.9% yield, but tighter than CoreWeave's five-year unsecured bond at about 10%.
SemiAnalysis says Firmus launched an 18,000-GB300 cluster in Melbourne in a self-built 42 MW data center.
SemiAnalysis says Firmus's Melbourne cluster was financed with a $10 billion facility led by Blackstone and supported by Coatue.
SemiAnalysis says Firmus expects $25–30 billion in customer revenue over six years from the project.
SemiAnalysis says Firmus announced a 600 MW firm-energy deal with Gunvor that will underwrite 1.2 GW of renewable development and 1.5 GWh of storage in South Australia by 2032.
SemiAnalysis says AMD began providing backstops in 2025.

SemiAnalysis says AMD offered AWS, OCI, DigitalOcean, Vultr, Tensorwave, Crusoe and other Neoclouds backstops beginning in 2025, under which AMD would rent unsold GPU capacity through long-term contracts for internal software development.
NVIDIA projected Q2 FY2027 revenue of approximately $91 billion, nearly 95% above the year-earlier quarter.
NVIDIA expected Q2 FY2027 non-GAAP gross margin of about 75%, compared with 72.7% a year earlier.
The author says NVIDIA made a $5 billion equity investment in Intel; no transaction date is stated.
The author estimates NVIDIA has roughly 81% of the AI chip market; the measurement period is not specified.
Bloomberg Intelligence forecasts a 27% CAGR for custom ASICs and a 16% CAGR for AI accelerators through 2033.
Broadcom guided Q3 AI semiconductor revenue to $16.0 billion, more than 200% higher year over year; the year is not specified.
The author cites estimates that memory will account for half of all data-center spending in calendar 2027.
Tom’s Hardware’s running tally reported that more than 75 US data center projects worth around $130 billion had been blocked or delayed so far in 2026.
The author estimates hyperscalers accounted for about 50% of NVIDIA's Q1 FY2027 data center revenue.
NVIDIA raised its quarterly dividend to $0.25 and authorized an additional $80 billion buyback.
Amazon disclosed that its Trainium business is now a multi-billion-dollar business; no period is specified.
The author says NVIDIA's China data center compute revenue is effectively zero; CFO Colette Kress said the future market there is close to $50 billion and losing it would be material.
Apple said it could no longer absorb rising memory and storage costs and announced price increases for some Macs and iPads.
SemiAnalysis claimed Nvidia scrapped its NVL72x2 back-to-back rack after hyperscaler customers pushed back.
Sharon AI is deploying up to 40,000 Grace Blackwell GB300 GPUs in Australia; Firmus is building a 360-megawatt DSX-aligned campus in Batam targeting up to 170,000 GPUs.
NVIDIA is conducting a multi-megawatt DSX Flex pilot with Emerald AI and Silicon Valley Power to adjust factory consumption in response to grid signals.

Jensen Huang said a 1-gigawatt AI factory that previously cost $20–30 billion now costs $50–60 billion and may soon cost $80–100 billion per gigawatt; he expects 100 gigawatts online before the end of the decade.
The analyst cites $25–30 billion in Firmus committed off-take and questions whether it will convert into recognized revenue on schedule.
Wall Street analysts expect Nvidia growth of 82% for the rest of 2026 and 41% for 2027; the passage does not specify the metric.
The average analyst projects Nvidia fiscal 2028 EPS of $12.76, for the fiscal year ending January 2028.
SemiAnalysis reported that Nvidia scrapped its planned NVL72x2 design, which would have placed two Oberon racks back to back.
SemiAnalysis reported that cloud providers and large data center operators objected to the NVL72x2 form factor and operational overhead.
SemiAnalysis reported that Nvidia canceled the Rubin Ultra version with four compute dies.
SemiAnalysis reported that only the two-die Rubin Ultra version remains and delivers roughly half the real-world compute performance of the canceled version.
SemiAnalysis reported that CPO-NVSwitch will not arrive until Nvidia's Feynman generation, the generation after next.
The report said Nvidia plans to sell more Oberon-Rubin racks in the existing form factor to make up for the shortfall.
Chinese executives surveyed said they plan to allocate 46% of their AI-accelerator budgets to domestic products over the 12 months after the survey.
The Bloomberg Intelligence survey reported that domestic products currently receive 30% of surveyed executives’ AI-accelerator budgets.
80% of surveyed Chinese executives said their total infrastructure spending was over budget in 2026, mostly because of AI-project costs.
Bloomberg Intelligence said its survey of 60 executives indicated progress in substituting domestic AI semiconductors for foreign ones, likely benefiting Huawei and Hygon.
The survey expected Nvidia’s market share in China to shrink as H20 chips became harder to find, Beijing urged technology firms not to use them, and local firms took over.
China was reported to be allocating roughly 2 trillion yuan (US$294 billion) to build data centres over the next five years.
Bloomberg News reported that domestic companies would supply at least 80% of core technologies, including chips, for the initiative.
Bloomberg reported that a global memory-chip shortage was likely to limit growth at Chinese AI firms such as SMIC and benefit ChangXin Memory Technologies.
The report said Chinese AI infrastructure bottlenecks were shifting from computing power to securing high-bandwidth memory supply.
SemiAnalysis said manufacturing issues would affect planned NVL576, which connects eight Oberon racks, and that it would likely be delayed or limited to small volumes.
SemiAnalysis separately reported around 2026-06-29 that Nvidia had canceled the four-die Rubin Ultra design in favor of a two-chiplet design, citing manufacturing execution concerns.
The report said the two-die Rubin Ultra offering would deliver about half the performance of the four-die design.
Tom's Hardware reported that NVL576, which links eight racks using co-packaged optics, was likely to be delayed or ship in low volume until the technology matures.
SemiAnalysis estimated that a fully production-ready co-packaged optics NVSwitch would arrive no earlier than the Feynman generation after Rubin.
The article reported that SemiAnalysis considered NVL576 likely to be delayed or to ship only in small volumes; the system links eight racks.

The article said Nvidia’s current-generation Rubin systems were in full production and planned to begin shipping in fall 2026 to eight major cloud partners, including AWS, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud.
SemiAnalysis estimated that Nvidia data-center compute revenue in the second half of FY2027 would be 20% above Wall Street’s then-current expectations.
SemiAnalysis alleged that Nvidia cancelled an alternative back-to-back rack design after operational pushback from hyperscale cloud clients.
SemiAnalysis claimed that a four-die configuration for the upcoming Rubin Ultra platform had been scrapped as the platform was downsized.
Analysts cited by Bloomberg said rumored technical setbacks could severely limit the scale-up capacity of Nvidia’s future hardware.
Morgan Stanley Research estimated the Vera Rubin VR200 NVL72 rack at about $7.8 million per unit, versus about $4 million for the GB300 NVL72.
Morgan Stanley estimated Nvidia would charge about $55,000 per Rubin GPU and $5,000 per Vera CPU when sold in volume.
Morgan Stanley estimated memory content at about $2 million per Vera Rubin rack, up 435% from the prior generation, with 54 terabytes of LPDDR5X and roughly $1 million or more of 3D NAND storage.
Morgan Stanley's bill-of-materials estimates put memory at 25–30% of VR200 cost versus 5–10% for GB200, and GPU share at about 51% versus 63%.
Morgan Stanley estimated that hyperscaler self-sourcing of certain memory modules could reduce a Vera Rubin rack's price to around $6.7 million.
Three Reuters sources said DeepSeek was designing its own AI chips specifically for inference; no completion date was reported.
Reuters sources said DeepSeek's chip development project was at an early stage as of 2026-07-07.
Reuters sources said DeepSeek had communicated with chip design firms, foundries and memory suppliers over the past year to support chip development.
Reuters sources said DeepSeek had increased recruitment of chip design engineers in recent months.
The article reported that Huawei held around half of China's AI chip market, valued at approximately US$50 billion; no valuation period was specified.
The article reported that OpenAI introduced its first inference chip, Jalapeno, with Broadcom in June 2026, and that Anthropic was reportedly considering developing its own AI chips.
DeepSeek launched V4, optimized for Huawei Ascend chips, in April 2026; Huawei said V4-Flash training also used Ascend processors.
The article reported that the DeepSeek V4 launch drove a surge in demand among Chinese technology companies for Huawei Ascend 950 chips; no size was given.
Reuters previously reported that DeepSeek was preparing a first funding round of US$7 billion at a valuation of US$52 billion to US$59 billion; the report date was not stated.
SemiAnalysis said the NVL576, designed to link eight racks, was likely delayed or limited to small initial volumes.
AMD CEO Lisa Su said customer engagement around MI450 Series and Helios was strengthening and leading-customer forecasts exceeded AMD's initial expectations.
Broadcom reported Q2 AI semiconductor revenue of $10.8 billion, up 143% year over year, and guided Q3 revenue to $16.0 billion.
Bloomberg Intelligence forecast a 27% CAGR for the custom ASIC market through 2033.
The article estimated NVIDIA's share of the AI chip market at approximately 81%.
McKinsey estimated the autonomous-driving market could reach roughly $300 billion to $400 billion by 2035.
The House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party proposed legislation to phase out Chinese-made lidar technology in the United States.
Anthropic said it was renting compute capacity from a SpaceX data center powered by over 220,000 Nvidia GPUs.
Alphabet is renting compute capacity that gives it access to 110,000 Nvidia GPUs.
Reuters reported, citing three unnamed sources, that DeepSeek is developing a custom chip for AI inference rather than model training.
Reuters reporting said DeepSeek's chip project had been underway for about a year, and that it was recruiting chip engineers and talking with foundries and memory suppliers.
DeepSeek reportedly closed its first outside funding round, raising $7.5 billion at a valuation above $50 billion.
Tencent, CATL and founder Liang Wenfeng were reported as backers of DeepSeek's $7.5 billion funding round.
Industry surveys indicate Chinese firms plan to allocate 46% of AI-accelerator budgets to domestic suppliers within 12 months, compared with roughly 30% currently.
Liang Wenfeng reportedly contributed roughly $2.9 billion to DeepSeek's funding round; most investors reportedly face a five-year lock-up under its limited-partnership structure.
Micron said tight memory-market conditions could last until 2028.
